Two critical vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) have been published. Both vulnerabilities carry a severe CVSS score of 9.2 (more technical details are in the


[Unit 42 Threat Brief](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cve-2026-109618-cve-2026-109619/) ).


This is not just another high-severity vulnerability disclosure, it marks the opening chapter in a massive acceleration of cyberthreats that will define the foreseeable future. Because PHP is widely used globally (by some estimates, more than half of all websites), the sheer scale of this is massive.


Navigating this new reality demands immediate imperatives, including continuous, proactive vulnerability discovery before adversaries weaponize code, and a modern defense strategy that pairs traditional patching with real-time virtual patching. At a footprint of 22 million exposed instances, relying on manual remediation cycles alone is not a viable defense.


For context, exposures are typically in the thousands, for example around 50,000 potentially vulnerable exposed instances for


[recent NetScaler vulnerabilities](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/netscaler-zero-days-exploited/) , and about 16,000 exposed instances of


[BeyondTrust](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/beyondtrust-cve-2026-1731/) , potentially vulnerable to CVE-2026-1731. Pervasive open-source software introduces an exposure footprint on an entirely different order of magnitude.


This situation illustrates what I shared in


[Defender’s Guide to the Frontier AI Impact on Cybersecurity](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/blog/2026/05/defenders-guide-frontier-ai-impact-cybersecurity-may-2026-update/) . We’re officially in a new reality, and this is going to be an ongoing cycle.


## An Accelerating Cycle


The latest frontier AI models are extraordinarily capable at finding vulnerabilities in code. We’ll see these models continue to surface critical issues at a pace faster than ever before.


But here’s the challenge: As soon as patches for vulnerabilities are available, attackers will reverse engineer the patch, locate the root flaw, and target them in near real time. It simply takes too long to apply patches to every system. This vulnerability deluge demands urgency and new technologies, such as virtual patching, are needed.


## What Organizations Should Do Now


### (1) Assess Your Open Source Inventory


Given the unprecedented speed at which new, critical vulnerabilities are being found with frontier AI, organizations need the ability to understand their true exposure at a moment’s notice. Attack surface management solutions have never been more critical for finding these blind spots across your entire codebase and supply chain. You can’t protect what you can’t see.


Additionally, services like[Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/blog/2026/09/introducing-unit-42-continuous-frontier-ai-defense/) put defender-grade AI models in the hands of defenders to find and fix vulnerabilities before attackers can weaponize them.


### (2) Prioritize Remediation Based on Reachability


You have to reduce what is reachable by attackers. You can't instantly patch everything everywhere, so prioritize what needs to be fixed first based on attack-path reachability. Secure what must be accessible to the public internet, and evaluate your environments to understand which of those exposed PHP instances carry the most immediate risk. For example, Cortex Xpanse and exposure management are great tools for determining reachability and automating remediation.


### (3) Secure your AI deployments


While not the main focus for these PHP vulnerabilities, rapid deployment of AI across organizations is expanding the attack surface. All AI deployments must be secure AI deployments.


### (4) Mitigate and Ensure Attack Protections


While you coordinate patching with your development teams, ensure best-in-class protections are in place to block the actual exploits. Mitigate against potential attacks immediately through proactive virtual patching and reducing overall exposure. Deploying high-fidelity virtual patches across your network and cloud security provides the mitigation layer necessary to give your teams the time they need to update the actual software safely.


Our new


[Frontier Virtual Patching](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/blog/network-security/harnessing-ai-for-prevention-introducing-frontier-virtual-patching/) capability delivered preemptive coverage for these PHP vulnerabilities ahead of today’s public disclosure. Additionally, Palo Alto Networks customers are protected from exploitation of these vulnerabilities by Advanced Threat Prevention available on our next-generation firewalls and Prisma Access.


### (5) Deploy Real-Time Security Operations


Autonomous AI-driven attacks will drive attack lifecycles to minutes requiring every SOC to achieve single-digit mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to respond (MTTR).


## The Path Forward: Institutionalize Defenses


This isn’t a one-and-done situation. With frontier AI compressing the patch-to-exploit window to minutes, assessing exposure, prioritizing reachability, mitigating and ensuring attack protections must become a continuous, automated motion.


This is a pivotal moment. While the scale of the challenge presented by frontier AI is real, I’m confident in our ability to solve it. Take the steps to secure your organization today, and build the foundation needed to ensure the advantage remains with the defender.
